en: The Questions of King Milinda, Chapter on Nibbāna, Section 6: The Question on the Heat of the Hell-Fires "Venerable sir," asked King Milinda, "is the fire of hell hot? "It is hot, great king. "But, venerable sir, does that fire of hell burn even now? "It does not burn, great king. "If it does not burn, venerable sir, how can it be said that the fire of hell is hot? "It is hot, great king, because of its potentiality (*sabhāva*). "But, venerable sir, what is the potentiality of that fire? "It has the potentiality to burn when it comes into contact with the body of one who has committed evil deeds. "But, venerable sir, if it burns when it comes into contact with the body of one who has committed evil deeds, why does it not burn even now? "It does not burn, great king, because it lacks fuel. "But, venerable sir, what is the fuel for that fire? "The fuel for that fire, great king, is the evil deeds themselves. "But, venerable sir, if the fuel consists of the evil deeds, why does it not burn even now? "It does not burn, great king, because those evil deeds have been exhausted. The King said:
"Venerable Nāgasena, you say:
'The fire of hell is far more intensely burning than ordinary fire; even a small stone [thrown] into ordinary fire..."
‘Even if cast in there, it would not go to destruction even after being cooked for a whole day;
yet a boulder the size of a gabled house, once cast into the fire of hell, goes to destruction in an instant’—I do not believe this statement, and you should rather say:
‘And those beings who have arisen there, though they are cooked in hell for many thousands of years, do not go to destruction.’”
“I do not believe that statement either, when it says they are going.
The Elder said:
“What do you think, Great King? As for those female crocodiles, female sharks, female turtles, female peacocks, and female pigeons—are they actually eating hard stones and gravel?”
“Yes, venerable sir, they eat them.
“But do those things undergo dissolution once they have entered into the interior of their bellies?
“Yes, venerable sir, they undergo dissolution.”
“But as for the embryo in their wombs, does that too go to destruction?
“No, venerable sir.
“For what reason?”
“I think, venerable sir, that they do not go to destruction because of the surplus of their karma.
“Just so, great king, because of the surplus of their karma, beings in hell who are being cooked in hell for many thousands of years do not go to destruction.
And this, great king, was said by the Blessed One:”
“Thus he does not die until that evil kamma has been exhausted.
“Give me a further simile,” [the king said].
“What do you think, great king? As for those lionesses, tigeresses, leopardesses, and bitches—do they eat hard bones and flesh?”
“Yes, venerable sir, they eat it.
“But when those things have gone inside their bellies, into the interior of the stomach, do they dissolve?
“Yes, venerable sir, they dissolve.”
“But as for the embryo within their wombs, does that too go to destruction?
“No, venerable sir.
“For what reason?”
“I think, venerable sir, that they do not go to destruction because of the surplus of their karma.
“Just so, great king, because of the surplus of their karma, beings in hell who are being cooked in hell for many thousands of years do not go to destruction.
“Give me a further simile.”
“What do you think, great king? As for those delicate women from among the Yonakas,
the Kṣatriyas, the Brāhmaṇas, and the householders— would they eat hard snacks consisting of meat?”
“Yes, venerable sir, they eat it.
“But do those things, having gone inside their bellies into the interior of the stomach, undergo dissolution?
“Yes, venerable sir, they undergo dissolution.”
“But as for the embryo within their wombs, does that too go to destruction?
“No, venerable sir.
“For what reason?”
“I think, venerable sir, that due to the surplus of karma, they do not go to destruction.
“Just so, great king, due to the surplus of karma, beings in hell who are being cooked in hell for many thousands of years do not go to destruction.
And this, great king, was said by the Blessed One:”
“Thus he does not die until that evil karma has been exhausted.
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena!
This is the sixth dilemma concerning the heat of the fires of hell.
